current.title: FutureEd Tracker Updated: 68 AI Education Bills Across 27 States with 10 Already Enacted in 2026
current.summary: FutureEd's 2026 state AI-in-education legislative tracker, refreshed May 18, now follows 68 bills across 27 states shaping how K-12 schools teach and govern AI, with 10 bills already signed into law—including Alabama's H.B. 329 requiring AI instruction as part of every student's high school graduation requirements.

current.title: Southern Illinois University Hosts Free All-Day AI Workshop to Equip Educators and Students for the AI Era
current.summary: Southern Illinois University Carbondale offered a free full-day 'AI @ SIUC' workshop on May 14 covering generative AI foundations, frontier models, and live student demonstrations, representing a growing university trend to translate AI research into hands-on professional development for teachers and regional communities.

current.title: Alabama Becomes Among First States to Require AI Instruction as a Formal High School Graduation Requirement
current.summary: Alabama's newly enacted H.B. 329 mandates that all high school students complete a computer science course that includes AI instruction before graduating, making Alabama one of the first states to formally embed AI literacy into K-12 graduation standards as national momentum builds toward the 2029 PISA AI literacy assessment.

archives.title: Stanford SCALE Initiative Releases First Rigorous Causal Evidence Review of AI Tools in K-12 Education
archives.summary: Stanford's SCALE Initiative published 'The Evidence Base on AI in K-12: A 2026 Review,' the first comprehensive analysis focusing specifically on causal-impact studies that can determine whether AI tools actually improved outcomes for students and educators.

archives.title: ISTE+ASCD and Google Launch Three-Year Partnership to Train Six Million U.S. Educators in AI Literacy
archives.summary: ISTE+ASCD and Google announced a landmark three-year partnership to deliver free, high-quality AI literacy training to six million K-12 teachers and higher education faculty across the United States, making it the largest educator AI upskilling initiative to date.

archives.title: FullScale and All4Ed Launch Rural AI Strategy Lab Bringing 13 School Teams Together to Integrate AI Thoughtfully
archives.summary: K-12 nonprofit FullScale partnered with advocacy organization All4Ed to launch a Rural AI Strategy Lab, uniting 13 rural school and district teams to collaboratively explore how AI can be integrated into teaching and learning in ways that are equitable and community-centered.

archives.title: Senators Schiff and Rounds Introduce Bipartisan LIFT AI Act to Bring AI Literacy to Every K-12 School
archives.summary: U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Mike Rounds introduced the bipartisan Literacy in Future Technologies (LIFT) Artificial Intelligence Act, which would fund AI literacy programs in K-12 schools nationwide to ensure students and educators are equipped to compete in an AI-driven economy.

archives.title: National Survey Finds U.S. Teachers Rapidly Adopting AI to Personalize Instruction and Cut Grading Time
archives.summary: A McKinsey-backed national survey reveals that the majority of U.S. teachers are now regularly using AI tools to differentiate learning, generate lesson materials, and automate routine grading, with middle and high school educators reporting the highest adoption rates across all subject areas.

archives.title: Educators and Researchers Call for Redesigning Classrooms Around AI-Powered Personalized Learning Models
archives.summary: A new report from Faculty Focus and leading education researchers argues that schools must move beyond simply adding AI tools to existing structures, instead fundamentally rethinking classroom design, pacing, and assessment to unlock the full potential of AI-driven personalized learning for every student.

archives.title: Parents Organize Against Unmonitored AI on School Chromebooks as Districts Weigh Access Controls
archives.summary: A growing wave of parents across the U.S. is pushing back after discovering that students as young as third grade have unrestricted access to generative AI tools like Google Gemini on school-issued Chromebooks, sparking calls for districts to implement clear age-appropriate guardrails before AI programs expand further.

archives.title: Ohio Becomes First State to Mandate Formal AI Policy for Every Public School District by July 2026
archives.summary: Ohio's Department of Education has required all traditional public school districts, community schools, and STEM schools to adopt an official AI use policy by July 1, 2026, making Ohio the first state to enforce a hard deadline for district-level AI governance backed by a statewide model policy framework.

archives.title: Adaptive AI Tutors Like Khanmigo Show Early Gains as 86% of U.S. Educational Organizations Now Use Generative AI
archives.summary: New data shows 86% of U.S. educational organizations have adopted generative AI—the highest rate of any industry—while platforms like Khan Academy's Khanmigo and other adaptive AI tutors are reporting measurable learning-gap improvements for K-12 students through personalized, real-time instruction.

archives.title: Wake County Freshman Falsely Accused of AI Cheating Sparks Petition for K-12 Detection Policies
archives.summary: A North Carolina high school freshman was wrongly flagged by three AI detection tools for an English assignment she wrote herself, prompting a student-led petition demanding that districts establish transparent AI detection guidelines and formal appeals processes before using such tools against students.

archives.title: SUNY Makes AI Literacy a General Education Requirement Across All 64 Campuses Starting Fall 2026
archives.summary: The State University of New York adopted a systemwide AI policy requiring all incoming undergraduates to complete AI literacy coursework starting Fall 2026, setting a major precedent for embedding foundational AI education into higher education curricula at scale.

archives.title: FutureEd Tracker: 53 State Bills in 25 States Shape Classroom AI as PISA Readies First AI Literacy Assessment for 2029
archives.summary: A new FutureEd legislative tracker reveals 53 active state bills across 25 states governing how AI is taught and used in K-12 schools, with urgency building around the news that PISA will for the first time test AI literacy among 15-year-olds worldwide in 2029.

archives.title: 31 States Introduce 134 AI Education Bills Targeting Student Data Privacy and Classroom Rules
archives.summary: A surge of 2026 state legislation is placing guardrails around AI in schools, with bills banning student data from being used to train AI models, requiring human oversight for high-stakes decisions, and adding AI instruction to graduation standards.

archives.title: Schools Worldwide Shift From AI Bans to Structured Deployment as UNESCO and EU Frameworks Take Hold
archives.summary: A 2026 review finds schools globally have moved past the ban-or-allow debate, now deploying AI as a productivity layer for teachers and administrators guided by UNESCO's generative AI guidance and the EU AI Act's phased rollout.

archives.title: Georgia and Mississippi Lead Push to Require AI Literacy Credits for High School Graduation
archives.summary: Multiple states are mandating AI instruction as part of computer science graduation requirements, signaling a national push to build foundational AI literacy among K-12 students before they enter the workforce.
